sections.heading: Data Matching and Entity Resolution with Edit Distance
Data Matching and Entity Resolution with Edit Distance
sections.evidence: This section examines how Levenshtein distance and related string-similarity methods contribute to record linkage and entity resolution, including noisy names and addresses, geographic records, patient identity, and privacy-preserving matching, while distinguishing textual similarity from evidence that two records represent the same real-world entity.
paragraphs: This section examines how Levenshtein distance and related string-similarity methods contribute to record linkage and entity resolution, including noisy names and addresses, geographic records, patient identity, and privacy-preserving matching, while distinguishing textual similarity from evidence that two records represent the same real-world entity.

01 Privacy-Preserving Record Linkage: Bloom Filters, PSI, Secure Computation & Attacks A rigorous guide to privacy-preserving record linkage: Bloom filters, q-gram encoding, cryptanalysis, private set intersection, secure multiparty computation, blocking, privacy leakage, and linkage evaluation. Article · 43 min read

02 Patient Identity Matching: Algorithms, MPI, Safety & Record Linkage A rigorous guide to patient identity matching: MPI and EMPI design, demographic comparators, probabilistic and referential matching, duplicate and overlay detection, FHIR $match, evaluation, safety, and privacy. Article · 40 min read

03 Name, Address & Place Matching: Normalization, Similarity & Entity Resolution A rigorous guide to matching names, addresses and places using edit distance, Jaro-Winkler, phonetic methods, structured parsing, transliteration, geography, blocking, and probabilistic evidence. Article · 32 min read

04 Entity Resolution & Record Linkage with Edit Distance: Models, Blocking & Decision Rules A rigorous guide to entity resolution and record linkage: Fellegi-Sunter matching, edit-distance comparators, blocking, probabilistic evidence, clustering, evaluation, and failure modes. Article · 28 min read
